description:
Your fingers are freezing, so why do they start warming themselves? Cyto breaks it down from the 6ix as the first real cold hits.

According to PubMed-indexed research: cold makes the blood vessels in your hands narrow (vasoconstriction), which cuts skin blood flow and skin temperature and makes your hands clumsier (Seeley 2026). Then, in the cold, vessels can open back up. That response is called cold-induced vasodilation or the hunting reaction (Weller 2023). In Weller 2023, 10 adults held a hand in about 4°C water for 30 minutes, twice, and finger temperature responses were measured.

The catch: these are small lab studies on healthy adults, mostly young men. The warm-up is not a reason to skip gloves.

Not medical advice. Fingers that stay white, numb or painful after warming up? See your doctor.
